integration_decision.name: REQUIRE_B_PHASE_WITNESS_TO_PREVENT_FALSE_GREEN_SERIALIZATION_CLASSIFICATION
integration_decision.new_finding: The prior acceptance branch 'B did not finish while A paused, then B finished after A release' is not evidence of safe serialization: a slow spawn/import/scheduler delay can produce the same ordering even with no publication lock. Treat this branch as INCONCLUSIVE absent positive evidence B entered the contested lock/critical section before A release; never count absence of overlap as a PASS.
integration_decision.no_network_contract: At exact SHA use spawn top-level children and T=1700000000000. A computes empty snapshot and pauses immediately before atomic_write_json(anata_latest.json), reporting A_prewrite payload lacks rowB. Parent appends PIT rowB (BTC ETF net_flow_usd; effective=T-2000, available=observed=T-1000). Start B with B_entered Event; instrument B_pre_first_publish Event after B has computed its rowB snapshot, and compact IPC (archive/scoring 1/1, role=scoring, effective.source_record_id=rowB). If B publishes all three files before A release, release A and require persisted cf-anata-handoff-v1 retains rowB; stale overwrite is RED. If B cannot reach/complete publication before A release, release A and require bounded completion but classify INCONCLUSIVE unless an explicit observed serialization-lock wait establishes the intended ordering. Do not infer serialization from elapsed time. Require A/B exitcodes, bounded Events/Queue/join, finally release/terminate/join, no network or sleeps. Three-file reader atomicity is out of scope without supported consumer contract. Run collect-only, targeted and full Capital Flow pytest at exact SHA; preserve logs.
